chunks: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Asad al-Asadi told us, saying: Uthman ibn Umar [ibn] Abi Ghailan al-Thaqafi and Isa ibn Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik al-Qurashi told us, saying: Abu Ibrahim al-Turjumani told us [saying: Sa'd ibn Sa'id al-Jarjani told us], saying: Nahshal ibn Sa'id told us, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said:
The nobles of my nation are the carriers of the Qur'an and the people of the night.

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ اللَّيْلِ: People of the night (those who pray night prayers)

ai.seo_question: Who are considered the nobles of the Muslim nation according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Ibn Abbas to emphasize that true nobility in the Ummah is defined by mastery of the Divine Word and devotion in prayer, rather than lineage or wealth. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on the integration of intellectual preservation (Huffaz) and spiritual discipline (Qiyam al-Layl) as the dual pillars of elite status. It serves as a practical guide for believers to elevate their standing through both recitation and contemplation.
